Angela observes that a drone is flying horizontally at a constant height of $5\,\text{m}$ above the ground. If the drone is flying in the opposite direction from Angela's location at a speed of $1\,\text{m/s},$ determine the rate at which the angle of elevation $\theta $ decreases at the moment when $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6}.$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14212968/assets/80b92831e73b31464fad3adeb1b2e3d9eed0a0df29e8f30b21bddd5f45bde230.png)

In the figure, $y$ is the drone's altitude, and $x$ is the horizontal distance between the drone and Angela. The quantity $y=5\,\text{m}$ does not change with time because the altitude of the drone is constant.

We wish to calculate $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.$ To do this, let's start by setting up a relation between $x$ and $y.$ Relative to the angle $\theta ,$ the sides $x$ and $y$ are the adjacent and opposite, respectively. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{y}{x} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{5}{x} \\ x & =5\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-5{csc}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given information, we have $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=1$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6}.$ Substituting this into the above, we reach

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =-5{csc}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\cdot \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} \\ 1 & =-5(2)^{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} \\ 1 & =-20\cdot \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =-0.05.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the angle of elevation is *decreasing* at a rate of $0.05$ radians per second.
